title: The three young men (Daniel 3)
hookLine: in the furnace they sing all ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord, a song the Church prays on Sundays
carry: all ye works, bless the lord

lines: A GOLDEN STATUE, AND A BAND.
cards: King Nabuchodonosor of Babylon sets up a golden statue, sixty cubits high, on a plain.
The order goes out: when you hear the music, the trumpet, the flute, the harp and all the rest, fall down and worship the statue, or be thrown into a burning furnace.

The band strikes up, and the whole empire goes down on its face. Except three young Jews in the king's service: Ananias, Azarias and Misael, given the Babylonian names Sidrach, Misach and Abdenago. They stay standing.
The king, furious, gives them one more chance: what god could deliver you out of my hand?

teach.b: Their answer doesn't bargain. Our God is able to save us from the furnace. But if he will not, know this, O king: we will not worship your gods.
The king has the furnace heated seven times hotter, so hot that the men who throw them in are killed by the flames. And the three walk around in the middle of the fire.

teach.h: A SONG IN THE GREEK DANIEL.
teach.b: In the Greek text of Daniel, which the Catholic Church receives as scripture, a long passage comes at this point: a prayer of Azarias in the fire, and then a song.
Bibles that follow the Hebrew and Aramaic text, as Protestant Bibles do, leave it out or print it separately among the Apocrypha.
The angel of the Lord comes down into the furnace, the text says, drives the flame out, and makes the middle of it like a cool, wet wind. And the three begin to sing.

In Latin it's the Benedicite, from its first word: bless. In the Douay-Rheims: "All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever." Then the song calls on everything by name.
Showers and dew. Fire and heat. Cold and frost.
Nights and days. Light and darkness. Mountains, seas, whales, birds, beasts.

teach.h: FIRE AND HEAT, BLESS THE LORD.
teach.b: From inside a furnace, they tell fire and heat to bless the Lord.

teach.h: ALL YE WORKS OF THE LORD, BLESS THE LORD.
teach.b: The Church still prays this canticle at Morning Prayer on Sundays and feasts.

how: The canticle of the three young men from Daniel 3 is prayed at Morning Prayer of the Liturgy of the Hours on Sundays and feasts, and it is a traditional prayer of thanksgiving for priests after Mass.

the blessing a priest gives at the end of Mass
a song calling every creature to bless God

games.q: you're one of the three. the king gives you a last chance: the music will play once more, and the furnace is ready. what do you say?
o: bow just this once; God will understand.
God is able to save us; but even if not, we won't worship your gods.
ask for time to think it over.
games.why: they don't bargain for rescue: even if not, they won't bow. thrown in, they walk in the fire and sing.

practice: Let your eyes land on one thing that is simply there, the light, a tree, rain, the cup in your hand, your own breathing, and name it. The song does exactly this, calling each thing to praise God just by being what it is.
If you pray, borrow its pattern: sun and moon, bless the Lord; nights and days, bless the Lord; if you don't, just be glad this one thing exists.

wordCard.voice: Benedicite. Latin for bless, the first word of the song of the three young men in the furnace, calling every creature to bless the Lord. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: bless ye (a command to many), the first word of the canticle; the Greek has eulogeite.
